narr: As high pressure slowly crept northward towards the Quad State region, ridging remained over the middle Mississippi River Valley. A slow-moving MCS moved through the northeastern half of the Quad State midday to near sunset. CAPE rose to 1000-2000J/kg in Southwest Indiana with effective bulk shear around 30kts. Extremely high moisture content with precipitable water values of 2.25in resulted in torrential rainfall rates in Southwest Indiana. Each of the six counties in Southwest Indiana reported flash flooding. In Gibson County, street flooding occurred in Francisco mid-late morning, with a gage reporting 4.25in of rain 3 miles NW of Francisco. Pike County had some of the longest lasting flooding as a widespread area saw 2-3.5 during the morning hours. Spencer County received 2.5-4 of rain in and around Rockport, with flooding there lingering towards sunset. More isolated flooding issues occurred in Posey, Vanderburgh, and Warrick Counties with Evansville area flooding generally on the north and east sides of the airport.
ev: Torrential rainfall with radar estimated hourly rainfall peaking at around 2/hr produced overflowing creeks which flooded yards.

Torrential rainfall produced flooding in much of Pike County with water across county roads, flooding of fields, and ditches and creeks overflowing banks. The report came in from southeastern Pike County which received 2-3.5 of rainfall during the morning with hourly rainfall peaking at a radar estimated 1.5-2.

Torrential rainfall resulted in flash flooding in northern portions of Evansville. Severe street flooding occurred on Kansas Road and Ashworth Drive, while nearby Green River Rd had areas of flooding. Floodwaters covered the roundabout at Oak Hill Rd and Hedden Rd. The Evansville airport received 2.16 of rain for the day, though radar estimates just north of the airport reach 3.
Flash flooding occurred in Petersburg. Radar estimated rainfall totals were approximately two inches. The report was submitted via mPING.

Flash flooding was reported on multiple roads in Pike County. These roads included IN-61 near County Rd 300N, County Rd 150N, and County Rd 125S near County Rd 125W. Radar estimates of morning rainfall in the area were 2-3.5 with peak hourly rainfall of 1.5-2 within an hour.

Flash flooding occurred at Heritage Hills Point West Trailer Park. Water was about 15in deep, and several trailers were surrounded by water. Nearby, part of the intersection of Lincoln Ave and Lenn Rd was covered.

Roads were submerged south of Richland City, including portions of CR 150 South and CR 900 W at W 70 N. Radar estimated rainfall was 2-3 during the afternoon, with most of the rain falling within 90min.
Several roads were flooded in Posey County as a result of torrential rainfall with radar estimated 3hr rainfall of 1.5-3.
Significant flash flooding occurred in Rockport due to hourly rainfall totals reaching radar estimated amounts of 2-2.5 in and around Rockport. The report was relayed on social media.
